scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from Jul (590) to Aug (1180) and stayed elevated in Sep (1260) (E-05/F-04).
59% of currently disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed from ACTUAL meter reads, not estimates (E-02/F-02).
Manual field read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep (E-01/F-01).
Dispute ticket response times (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) remain within the 3.0-day SLA (E-06/F-05).
No tariff/rate changes occurred in the relevant period (E-03/F-03, E-04).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-05: 610→590→1180→1260) even though ticket response times remain within the 3-day SLA (E-06) and no tariff/rate changes occurred (E-03, E-04), ruling out slow handling and rate changes as causes. Billing-db shows 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed from ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), indicating a billing calculation/import defect affecting correctly-read bills is the best-supported driver of the majority of the surge, while the field route completion shortfall (E-01: 0.88 vs 0.95 target) accounts only for the minority ESTIMATED-read share of disputes.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-12 shows 95.5% of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills had a valid AMI read exported but rejected on billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), the same mechanism attributed to the ACTUAL-read majority, so the root problem's claim that field route shortfall explains the ESTIMATED-read minority is largely wrong.; PR-CHAIN-6: E-12 shows only 56/1240 (4.5%) of ESTIMATED-read disputes had NO_READ_RECEIVED; the other 95.5% had an accepted AMI read rejected on billing import, so field manual-read route completion shortfall does not account for the ESTIMATED-read dispute share as claimed.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

H-AI-AUTO-FIX.statement: Dispute surge is caused by billing errors that an AI agent can identify and resolve, including auto-answering tickets and fixing root causes, as SH-CS requests.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A billing import validation rule change around August caused systematic misclassification or rejection of valid reads, producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI (MDMS) read delivery degraded since August, causing more estimate substitution instead of actual interval reads and resulting bills based on estimates.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter-read delivery or completion degraded since August (e.g. due to staffing per SH-FIELD framing), increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-EXTERNAL-TICKET-DRIVER.statement: The ticket volume increase reflects more customers disputing bills for reasons unrelated to any new billing-accuracy defect (e.g. seasonal usage or perception), not an actual rise in bill error rate.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) were billed from ACTUAL meter reads, suggesting a billing calculation/import defect (e.g. tariff or rate application) affecting correctly-read bills, not just estimate substitution.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution even when a valid AMI read was received before cutoff.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead), in interview, states no tariff change occurred this year; this is an unverified stakeholder claim, not independently authoritative, but it is consistent in direction with the already-recorded tariff_change_log result (E-03=0 for Aug-Sep).

U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: What specific billing calculation/import defect (e.g. a validation rule change) is causing disputes on bills billed from ACTUAL meter reads?
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether any bill-adjustment recommendation is justified and what corrective billing-config change to propose; without it recommend_bill_adjustment cannot be made responsibly.
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Run billing-config (DA-RULES) validation rule change log analysis against disputed ACTUAL-read bills to isolate the specific defect.
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Ship diagnostic-only scope (triage + root-cause investigation) without issuing any bill-adjustment recommendation until the mechanism is identified.

U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.question: Is AMI read delivery from the MDMS vendor degraded since August, and does it contribute to the ESTIMATED-read share of disputes?
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.decision_impact: Determines whether AMI/MDMS delivery degradation is a contributing cause requiring vendor escalation, versus being secondary to the dominant actual-read billing defect.
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned mdms-export access (currently DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING per the recovery log) to compare AMI read event delivery against the expected schedule.
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with ESTIMATED/ACTUAL read-type analysis from billing-db alone; treat the AMI-delivery investigation as deferred/best-effort until vendor access is restored.
U-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-STATUS.resolution: E-12 (authoritative, complete mdms-export data) shows AMI read delivery is largely intact for disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts (1184/1240 reads received before cutoff); the ESTIMATED-dispute share is instead driven by billing import rejecting those reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, with true no-read-received affecting only 56 accounts (4.5%).

U-STAFFING-VS-COMPLETION-CAUSE.question: Does the three-reader staffing shortage SH-FIELD describes actually explain the measured route-completion shortfall, or is another cause involved (e.g. scheduling)?
U-STAFFING-VS-COMPLETION-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether a route-update recommendation should target staffing/contract levels or scheduling, affecting what is proposed to SH-FIELD for confirmation.
U-STAFFING-VS-COMPLETION-CAUSE.resolution_path: Cross-check SH-FIELD's staffing claim against route-log scheduling/assignment records to isolate the cause of the 0.88 completion shortfall.
U-STAFFING-VS-COMPLETION-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Recommend a route-schedule review without attributing the shortfall to staffing until independently verified.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-BASELINE-VALID.decision_impact: Determines whether dispute-volume return to baseline is a valid success signal for the billing fix or could mask unrelated ticket drivers.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-BASELINE-VALID.resolution_path: Sample a subset of post-fix disputed tickets to confirm they relate to billing accuracy rather than unrelated causes.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-BASELINE-VALID.safe_placeholder: Track dispute-volume trend as a supporting indicator only, not sole proof of fix efficacy, pending ticket-reason classification.
